questions.stem: What is a Key Performance Indicator (KPI)?
options: A measurable value used to evaluate how effectively an individual, team, department or organisation is achieving its objectives
A qualitative statement of where an organisation wants to go
Any metric an organisation happens to generate
A management philosophy introduced by Peter Drucker
A quarterly goal-setting cycle popularised by Google
questions.explanation: A KPI is a measurable value used to evaluate how effectively an individual, team, department or organisation is achieving its objectives. Objectives define the destination; KPIs measure progress towards it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for a metric to qualify as a KPI?
options: It must be directly linked to a strategic objective
It must be generated automatically by a software dashboard
It must be clearly measurable
It must be regularly monitored
It must be capable of influencing decisions
questions.explanation: A KPI must be directly linked to a strategic objective, clearly measurable, regularly monitored and capable of influencing decisions. Being produced automatically by a dashboard is not one of the qualifying criteria.

questions.stem: Why is 'the number of emails sent' described as merely a metric rather than a KPI, while 'customer retention rate' may be a KPI?
options: Because emails cannot be counted accurately
Because retention rate is a financial figure and emails are not
Because customer retention rate can be tied to a strategic priority such as customer loyalty, whereas email volume does not focus attention on what truly matters
Because KPIs must always be expressed as percentages
Because email metrics belong only to operational teams
questions.explanation: Not every metric is a KPI. The word 'Key' means the metric must focus attention on what truly matters, so customer retention rate may be a KPI when customer loyalty is a strategic priority, while the number of emails sent is simply a metric.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an operational KPI?
options: Market share
Revenue growth
Profitability
Order processing time
Return on investment
questions.explanation: Operational KPIs track daily performance, such as order processing time or system uptime. Revenue growth, market share and profitability are strategic KPIs, and return on investment is a financial KPI.

questions.stem: In the relationship between MBO, OKR and KPI, which statement is correct?
options: KPI defines the philosophy, MBO defines goal cycles, OKR defines measurable indicators
OKR defines the philosophy, KPI defines goal cycles, MBO defines measurable indicators
KPIs cannot be used inside either MBO or OKR frameworks
MBO and OKR are both types of KPI
MBO defines the philosophy, OKR defines structured goal cycles, and KPI defines measurable indicators
questions.explanation: In simple terms, MBO defines the philosophy, OKR defines structured goal cycles and KPI defines measurable indicators. KPIs can be used within both MBO and OKR frameworks.

questions.stem: A call centre measures only the number of customer calls each employee handles. According to the guidance on KPI design, what is the likely problem?
options: It measures activity rather than impact, which may encourage employees to rush conversations instead of solving problems
It is a strategic KPI wrongly used at operational level
It cannot be displayed on a dashboard
It is too difficult to measure
It is a financial KPI rather than a customer KPI
questions.explanation: Poorly designed KPIs can create harmful behaviour. Measuring only the number of calls handled may encourage employees to rush conversations instead of solving problems effectively. A good KPI measures impact, not just activity.

questions.stem: In the Grade 7 classroom example for KPIs, the teacher's goal is that the class should improve in Mathematics. What is the KPI used to measure this goal?
options: The number of maths lessons taught
The average maths test score of the class
The number of students in the class
The number of homework sheets handed out
The teacher's annual appraisal rating
questions.explanation: The teacher defines the KPI as the average maths test score of the class. If the average rises from 70 to 80 per cent during the year, the KPI shows progress; without measuring it, improvement would be hard to confirm.

questions.stem: Which category of KPI measures productivity and quality?
options: Financial KPIs
Customer KPIs
Process KPIs
Strategic KPIs
Operational KPIs
questions.explanation: Process KPIs measure productivity and quality. Financial KPIs measure cost efficiency and return on investment, customer KPIs measure satisfaction and retention, strategic KPIs measure long-term success and operational KPIs track daily performance.

questions.stem: If a person aims to read 12 books in a year, which KPI would show whether they are on schedule?
options: The total number of books owned
The number of pages in each book
The average price paid per book
The number of books read per month
The number of bookshops visited
questions.explanation: For a personal goal of reading 12 books in a year, the KPI could be the number of books read per month. Tracking that number shows whether the reader is on schedule.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a characteristic of a well-designed KPI?
options: Aligned with strategy
Clearly defined
Measurable
Realistic
Reviewed only once at the end of the year
questions.explanation: A well-designed KPI is aligned with strategy, clearly defined, measurable, realistic and understandable. KPIs are meant to be regularly monitored, typically on dashboards reviewed by leadership, not checked only once a year.
